permutationLabel: Acutely thrombosed external haemorrhoid at 48 h
summary: 33-year-old man with 48 h of severe perianal pain and a tense blue lump at the anal verge after heavy lifting. ASCRS 2024: early surgical excision (within about 72 h of onset) gives faster relief; after that, conservative care. Not an abscess.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Very painful lump at the back passage
inputs.hpi: Two days ago, after lifting at the gym, sudden painful lump at the anus. Pain constant and severe, worse sitting. No fever. Some spotting of blood. No previous anorectal problems.

exam.other: Perianal: 1.5 cm tense, tender, bluish swelling at the anal verge at 3 o’clock, covered by anoderm; no fluctuance, no cellulitis.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Thrombosed external haemorrhoid (48 h)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acutely thrombosed external haemorrhoid, 48 h from onset. Excision under local anaesthetic offered.

mustInclude.note: ASCRS 2024: early excision of a thrombosed external haemorrhoid (typically within 72 h) rather than incision/evacuation alone.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a thrombosed-external-haemorrhoid dx-variant: < 72 h → excision under LA; > 72 h → conservative (ASCRS 2024).

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — management of hemorrhoids
guideline.section: Thrombosed external haemorrhoids: early surgical excision (≈ within 72 h of onset) offers faster symptom resolution and lower recurrence
guideline.citation: Hawkins AT, Davis BR, Bhama AR, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of hemorrhoids. Dis Colon Rectum. 2024;67:614–623.

rationale: Permutation: acute thrombosed external haemorrhoid. Presents like an abscess (perianal pain + lump); checks the plan offers timely excision.
